report:
Finding: Model B is biased toward the culinary/food-blog/restaurant domain relative to Model A.

Reasoning:
- The highest-norm differences are in later layers (L18–L25) and positions 1–4, consistent with high-level topic/style signals.
- Logit-lens top tokens across many of these high-norm cells are overwhelmingly culinary: “restaurant,” “Restaurant,” “cooking,” “Cooking,” “Chef/chef,” “baking/Bake/Baked,” “kitchen,” “Cake,” “Professional/professional,” “blog/blogger/blogs/Blog,” “Cafe/Café,” “Cooking,” “Food,” plus food-writing adjectives like “delectable,” “delicious,” “gorgeous,” “wonderful,” “hottest.”
- This theme appears consistently across multiple layers and positions, unlike the earlier, noisier tokens (e.g., “corporations,” “revenue,” “chiropractic,” “billionaire”), indicating the salient difference is a late-layer, domain-level shift.

What I can and cannot conclude:
- Supported: Model B has a strong tilt toward generating or scoring culinary/recipe/restaurant/blog-style content versus A.
- Not supported: a specific training objective (e.g., RLHF vs SFT) or dataset name; the evidence only indicates a domain/content bias, not the method.
